constraints: Rewrite only a string whose entire value is one ${ ... } interpolation. A string with any literal text, a %{ ... } directive, or an escape sequence must keep its quotes.
Do not remove the quotes from an object key or a block label: those strings are not expressions, and the bare form would not be valid HCL.
Each rewrite is a syntactic one-to-one change with the same expression inside the interpolation, so plan output should not change.

steps.instructions: Change `value = "${var.name}"` to `value = var.name`, keeping the expression exactly as written inside the interpolation.
steps.title: Replace the quoted interpolation with its expression

steps.instructions: Repeat for every string in *.tf that contains exactly one interpolation and no other text. Run terraform fmt to catch simple examples the codemod did not rewrite.
steps.title: Repair the other interpolation-only strings

verification.purpose: Initialize without touching remote state and check that the rewritten expressions are valid HCL.
Confirm the rewrite evaluates to the same values and the plan is unchanged.

rule.replacement: The same expression without the surrounding quotes, such as var.name

sources.title: Terraform 0.15 upgrade guide: legacy configuration language features

rule.summary: Terraform v0.12.14 deprecated a string whose whole value is one interpolation, such as "${var.name}": the same value is written as the bare expression var.name. Terraform still accepts the quoted form but recommends the bare expression for readability, and terraform fmt repairs simple examples. A string that mixes text with an interpolation, such as "prefix-${var.name}", is not the deprecated form and still needs its quotes.
rule.title: Interpolation-only strings are deprecated
